intro: Six things a locus must keep apart. A claim in one ring is not a claim in the next.

steps.caption: A locus observes something. The observation may be stale, forged or partial — it is in the second ring, not the first.
It forms a belief. Belief is not observation: the ring narrows and the claim must earn its way in.
steps.takeaway: Establish, never know: an observation survives staleness and forgery checks before it becomes a belief.

steps.caption: Understanding is narrower still — the belief connected to why. Intent narrower again. And what it may alter is the smallest ring: scoped authority.
Agent Omniscience is a claim that jumps rings: 'I observed it, so I may alter it.' Refused — the rings between were skipped.
steps.takeaway: A claim is never promoted from one register to the next without evidence for the step.

steps.caption: The epistemic rung of the governance ladder is where 'do we know enough?' is asked; a Bot knows its projection, not the world.
steps.takeaway: STALE ≠ UNESTABLISHED: an old observation is still established; an unestablished one was never an observation at all.
